Penurious

puh-NYUR-ee-us · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Penurious is extremely stingy, especially despite having enough money to spend.

The landlord was so penurious that he refused to call a plumber, patching the leaking pipe himself with tape.

Worked Example

The company's penurious founder still photocopied both sides of every page to save paper, even after the business went public.

Photocopying both sides of every page to save paper, even after going public, is exactly the extreme, joyless stinginess penurious describes.

How Penurious Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

penny-pinching

penny-pinching: unwilling to spend money even when able to

tightfisted

tightfisted: reluctant to part with money

Antonyms

generous

generous: willing to give or spend freely

How Strong Is It? — sparing → penurious → avaricious

sparing vs. penurious

sparing vs. penurious: Being sparing simply means spending carefully to avoid waste -- a mild, sensible habit; penurious pushes that same instinct into extreme, joyless stinginess.

avaricious vs. penurious

avaricious vs. penurious: Avaricious adds an active hunger to acquire more wealth, while penurious is narrowly about refusing to let go of money one already has.

Build the Word

The pieces

Put it together

Put it together: Penurious traces to Latin penuria, 'want, need, scarcity' -- describing someone who acts as though scarcity is always just around the corner, even when it isn't.

Use the root in a new word: penury

Use the root in a new word: penury: The same penuria root gives us the rarer noun penury, meaning extreme poverty -- penurious describes the penny-pinching behavior someone shows, whether or not they are actually poor.

Word Building

Word Choice

Penurious focuses on stinginess as a behavior, often surprising precisely because the person could easily afford to spend. It is a close relative of Impecunious (taught earlier in this course), which instead describes someone who genuinely has no money at all -- Impecunious is about lacking funds; Penurious is about refusing to use funds one has.
